title: Guidelines for Using a Salt:Chloroform Wash to Clean Up HMW DNA for PacBio
author: Miguel Flores
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcuriwv6
materials: Add the following reagents to TUBE 1 : gDNA in EB
Invert the tube 20 times to mix.

steps.title: Adjust DNA volume and label
steps.instruction: Bring the volume of the high‑molecular‑weight DNA up to 200 µL with Elution Buffer (EB) and label the tube as TUBE 1.

steps.title: Prepare Buffer A
steps.instruction: Prepare 5 M NaCl solution (Buffer A); use 500 µL of this buffer for each sample.

steps.title: First phenol‑chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL of Phenol:Chloroform:Isoamyl Alcohol (25:24:1, pH 8) to TUBE 1, mix, then spin at maximum speed (≥10 g) for 10 min at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Carefully transfer the aqueous layer to a clean 2 mL microcentrifuge tube without disturbing the interphase and label it TUBE 2.

steps.title: Second phenol‑chloroform extraction with Buffer A
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL of Buffer A (from step 2) to the original TUBE 1, mix, and spin at maximum speed (≥10 g) for 10 min.

substeps.instruction: Again, carefully transfer the aqueous layer to TUBE 2 without disturbing the interface.

steps.title: Verify aqueous volume
steps.instruction: Measure the volume in TUBE 2; it should be close to 800 µL.

steps.title: Chloroform‑isoamyl wash
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of Chloroform:Isoamyl Alcohol (24:1) to TUBE 2, mix, and spin at maximum speed (≥10 g) for 10 min.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the aqueous layer to a clean 2 mL tube and label it TUBE 3.

steps.title: Low‑ethanol polysaccharide precipitation
steps.instruction: Add 0.3 × the volume of TUBE 3 of 99.99 % ethanol (calculate: volume_T3 × 0.3 = µL ethanol), mix, and spin at maximum speed (≥10 g) for 15 min.

substeps.instruction: Remove the supernatant without disturbing the polysaccharide pellet (the pellet may be invisible) and place the supernatant into a clean 2 mL tube labeled TUBE 4; measure its volume. TUBE 4 now contains the gDNA.

steps.title: Ethanol precipitation of gDNA
steps.instruction: Add 1.7 × the volume of TUBE 4 of 99.99 % ethanol (calculate: volume_T4 × 1.7 = µL ethanol) and mix.

substeps.instruction: If the final volume exceeds 2 mL, split the mixture into two tubes.
Spin at maximum speed (≥10 g) for 15 min, then discard the supernatant without disturbing the DNA pellet.

steps.title: First 70 % ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of 70 % ethanol to the DNA pellet, mix gently, and spin at maximum speed (≥10 g) for 15 min.

substeps.instruction: Discard the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Second 70 % ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Add another 500 µL of 70 % ethanol to the DNA pellet, mix, and spin at maximum speed (≥10 g) for 15 min.

substeps.instruction: Carefully remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Remove residual ethanol
steps.instruction: Perform a quick spin to collect any remaining ethanol at the bottom of the tube and remove it with a P20 pipette tip.

steps.title: Air‑dry DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Let the DNA pellet air‑dry for 5 min at room temperature, taking care not to overdry.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA in Tris‑HCl
steps.instruction: Resuspend the DNA pellet in 100 µL of 10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 8; incubate at 4 °C with gentle mixing overnight. Store at 4 °C for use within one week or at –80 °C for long‑term storage. If processing two technical replicates, resuspend both pellets together with a single 100 µL aliquot of 10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 8.
